text:
Stephanie Nguyen: For enterprise platform teams, what scenarios are we prioritizing for the standard demo tenant? We can’t do 6 things live. Need the 3-4 that land best + fit in 20 mins.

Markus Klein: +1. Platform eng folks don’t care about “cool prompts”, they want: reliability under load, controls, and what happens when stuff breaks.

Soojin Lee: From deck POV, we need a clean narrative arc. If we bounce around too much (chat -> tools -> embeddings -> routing -> console), it feels like a feature dump.

Simran Kaur: Agree. If we optimize for platform persona:
1) “Same API across hosted/dedicated/private” (deployment flexibility)
2) “Smart routing + fallback policy” (reliability)
3) “Cost/latency levers + observability” (unit economics + proof)
Then optionally a 60s “developer happy path” at the start.

Stephanie Nguyen: What do we cut then? Tool calling + structured output? I know some AEs love that.

Markus Klein: Tool calling is great for ML/app teams, but platform folks will ask “how do you keep it up + keep spend predictable.”

Renee Sullivan: Could do a 2-min opener that’s just streaming chat + shows the API is normal. Then pivot immediately to “why Redwood in prod.”

Soojin Lee: That’s consistent with the deck flow I’m drafting:
- Slide: 2-min API “hello world” (streaming)
- Slide: routing policy + fallback (show live)
- Slide: cost/latency dashboard + tracing (show live)
- Slide: deployment modes (talk + 1 diagram, no live)

Lukas Meyer: For EMEA / platform teams, data residency question comes up almost immediately. If we wait until the end to mention regions/VPC, we lose them.

Markus Klein: Good call. Maybe we “pre-answer” residency + isolation in the first 5 mins, even if we don’t deep dive.

Simran Kaur: We can do: intro -> “where does this run” slide -> then live scenarios. Otherwise we’ll get derailed mid-demo with security questions.

Marissa Cole: On console clickpath: if we do routing/fallback live, we need it to be dead simple (one saved view). Dry run last week had too many clicks.

Mina Haddad: For routing demo, what’s the cleanest failure mode? We can simulate primary model capacity constraint (force 503 from route A) and show auto-fallback to compatible variant. But we need a safe “toggle” so it’s repeatable.

Markus Klein: Ideal: a single switch like “degrade primary” or “simulate capacity.” If we can’t do that, we can still show fallback using a preconfigured policy + run the request against a “flaky” route.

Stephanie Nguyen: I want something we can explain without saying “we hacked the demo.” Prospects smell that.

Simran Kaur: We can narrate it as “policy test.” Like: “We run an intentional chaos check to validate our fallback policy.” That’s believable for platform teams.

Renee Sullivan: + we can have Plan B if the failure doesn’t trigger: show the routing policy config and then show historical request traces where fallback happened (pre-seeded). Not ideal but keeps narrative.

Soojin Lee: Timing: if we do both routing/fallback + cost/latency console live, that’s already ~10-12 mins with narration. Add 2 mins API + 3 mins deployment/security and we’re at 15-17. Leaves some room for questions.

Lukas Meyer: That works. Please make sure we have 1 slide / talking point on EU-only routing / region pinning even if demo tenant is US-based.

Markus Klein: So do we agree: platform persona default path =
(1) quick API streaming request (hosted)
(2) routing + fallback policy test (reliability)
(3) cost/latency + token breakdown dashboard (economics)
(4) deployment modes + “how to go private / dedicated” (flexibility)
And we cut tool calling / structured output unless asked.

Stephanie Nguyen: Yes. I’d still like a “if asked” branch: structured output in 90 seconds to show we’re not behind on app features.

Renee Sullivan: I can add a sidebar to the talk track: “If they’re an app team / ML eng, swap in structured output scenario.”

Marissa Cole: For console demo, I’ll work with Chloe to create a saved view that opens directly to:
- last 15 mins latency p50/p95
- token cost breakdown by route
- error panel + fallback counts
One URL.

Mina Haddad: I’ll sync with Simran on the fallback policy so it’s deterministic enough. We should decide on the exact “trigger” and expected trace.

Soojin Lee: I’ll update the deck outline to move “where this runs / isolation” earlier (after API hello world). Also will add a callout: “No customer data in demo tenant; sanitized logs.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect. Can someone write down the “platform persona path” in one place so AEs stop improvising?

Markus Klein: I’ll drop it in the master script doc and pin it. Also will add a “don’t do these live unless asked” list (tools, rerank, embeddings).

Renee Sullivan: Action items I heard:
- Mina + Simran: define fallback trigger + expected behavior
- Marissa: saved console view + clickpath
- Soojin: reorder deck + add residency/isolation early
- Markus: update talk track + platform persona default path

Stephanie Nguyen: :thumbsup: Thanks all. Goal is a repeatable 20-min version that doesn’t rely on SE magic.

Lukas Meyer: +1. If we nail this, it’ll reduce the “EMEA demo went sideways on residency Qs” problem.

Soojin Lee: Will share a draft outline EOD for review.

Markus Klein: Cool. I’ll schedule a dry run focused only on platform persona flow once the console view is ready.
